title: Black Box Recovery
story:
After the crash, some of the black box's files survived and some didn't. Check each one the rescue team asks about.

Input: `n` (1–20), then n file names. The judge puts the surviving files next to your program; the others simply don't exist.

Output, one line per name in order:
- `NAME: missing` if it can't be opened,
- otherwise `NAME: L lines, W words`.

Then a last line `found F of N files`.

A **line** ends with a newline; a last line without one still counts (an empty file has 0 lines). A **word** is a run of characters that aren't spaces, tabs or newlines. Watch out: some lines are very long.

hints: fopen each name in turn; NULL means missing. Count how many opened for the last line, and fclose every file you opened.
Reading lines with a small fgets buffer miscounts the very long lines. Reading one character at a time with `int c = fgetc(f)` until `c == EOF` avoids buffers completely.

Count `\n` characters for lines, plus one if the file didn't end with `\n` (remember the last character you saw). A word starts whenever a non-space character follows a space or the start of the file: `isspace(c)` checks for space, tab and newline.
